claims.text: A Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil reduces the incidence of major cardiovascular events in persons at high cardiovascular risk compared to a control diet (hazard ratio 0.70).
A Mediterranean diet supplemented with mixed nuts reduces the incidence of major cardiovascular events in persons at high cardiovascular risk compared to a control diet (hazard ratio 0.72).
No diet-related adverse effects were reported for the Mediterranean diet interventions during the trial.

evidence.description: Multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio was 0.70 (95% CI, 0.54 to 0.92) with 96 events in the olive oil group versus 109 events in the control group over a median follow-up of 4.8 years.
Multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio was 0.72 (95% CI, 0.54 to 0.96) with 83 events in the nut group versus 109 events in the control group over a median follow-up of 4.8 years.
Trial monitoring reported no diet-related adverse effects among the 7,447 enrolled participants.

methodologies.name: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of Mediterranean Diets
methodologies.description: Participants at high cardiovascular risk without baseline cardiovascular disease were randomly assigned to a Mediterranean diet with extra-virgin olive oil, a Mediterranean diet with mixed nuts, or a control diet with fat reduction advice, receiving regular dietary education sessions.
conditions: Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil
Mediterranean diet supplemented with mixed nuts
Control diet (advice to reduce dietary fat)
